name: TwoTrees TTS-55 10W
tagline: 10W Ultra-budget diode with surprising build quality for the price
tldr: TwoTrees TTS-55 10W is the 10W SKU on the TwoTrees twotrees tts 55 line. TwoTrees undercuts Atomstack and Ortur on price while offering a usable 5. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: High-quality hobby and light-business engraving with light, slow cutting

priceRange.note: 10W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Cheapest TTS-55 configuration with real cutting ability: $179–279
Basswood up to 5 mm in our profile, against thin stock on the original 5W machine
Finest spot of the TTS-55 line in our profile (~0.08 mm)
cons: Slow fills in our benchmark: ~28–43 min for a 10 × 10 cm photo at 3–8 mm/s
Cutting a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes ~14–24 min
Older, no-frills frame (as Tom's Hardware's review put it) with a 300 × 300 mm bed
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 10W SKU on TwoTrees TTS-55. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Run material test grids at engraving speeds first. Add air assist for light cuts. If cut jobs exceed ~30% of your week, open the higher-watt profile on this site and compare times.

editorialDepth.advantages: TwoTrees TTS-55 10W suits makers who sell marks, photos, and gifts more than daily panel cutting. Reasonable open-frame entry price.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if you already quote 5 mm+ cutting in production: see 20W or 40W in the line. Not for cast acrylic or bare metal without spray.

faq.question: How does the TTS-55 10W compare with the original 5W TTS-55?
faq.answer: The TTS-55 was launched around a 5W laser; Tom's Hardware's review found it could still cut 8 mm light plywood with patience. The 10W module roughly doubles the power on the same 300 × 300 mm frame, and our profile lists basswood up to 5 mm as a practical limit.

faq.question: Is the TTS-55 10W fast enough for engraving orders?
faq.answer: For occasional orders, yes; for volume, no. Our benchmark puts a 10 × 10 cm filled photo at ~28–43 min, against ~18–28 min with the 20W module. Text and line art run much faster than full photo fills.

faq.question: Should I buy the 10W or go straight to the 20W?
faq.answer: If your budget stops at about $200, the 10W ($179–279) is a fair starter. TwoTrees sells a 20W module for the TTS-55 at $359 (October 2026), so if cutting matters, a machine that already ships with 20W is cheaper than upgrading later.

standoutFeatures.title: Budget entry with cutting
standoutFeatures.body: $179–279 for a 10W diode on the 300 × 300 mm TTS-55 frame, with basswood up to 5 mm in our profile.

standoutFeatures.title: Finest spot of the line
standoutFeatures.body: ~0.08 mm spot in our profile, the tightest of the TTS-55 tiers, which suits text and line art.
